items.title: AISI 红队论文：攻击策略选择会让 LLM 监视器评估结果失真
items.description: 英国 AI Security Institute 发布论文，测试合成攻击生成方式对监视器评估的影响。评估一个 OpenAI 前生产监视器时，同一监视器对不同攻击策略的漏报率从 0.2%（基础提示）到 23%（转录编辑）不等，优化程度也会显著改变结果。作者指出合成转录只是真实有害行为代理，其代表性难以证明，仅凭监视器评估不足以保证部署安全，需辅以能力限制、人工在环和沙箱等分层防护。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/tl8v9gto8rd3e4x40xfbljj13

items.content: 就在刚刚，Lean 和 Mathlib 社区发布联合声明，宣布正式认证 Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 提交的黎曼猜想形式化证明，并表示对其正确性具有充分信心。 更引人关注的是，Alpöge 此前透露，这项研究由他与 AI 模型 Claude 合作完成。在证明接近终点时，Claude 展现出的数学推理能力，甚至超出了他的预期。 11 月 20 日，Alpöge 在个人网站公布研究成果，宣称解决了著名的黎曼猜想（Riemann Hypothesis），同时取得了涉及广义黎曼猜想（Generalized Riemann Hypothesis）的结果。 它涉及黎曼 ζ 函数非平凡零点的分布，核心命题是所有非平凡零点的实部是否都等于 1/2。由于这一问题与素数分布密切相关，过去一个多世纪，无数数学家尝试攻克，却始终未能找到严格证明。 马斯克也发文感叹，证明黎曼猜想能够让大量此前依赖该猜想成立的数学结论摆脱条件限制，成为无条件成立的定理，并称其为超级智能取得的又一项惊人成就。 他曾尝试让 Claude 将证明整理成人类能够阅读的文字版本，结果生成的草稿超过 25 万页，庞大到连他本人都认为难以阅读。如此惊人的篇幅，甚至被部分网友戏称为一场针对数学界的「DDoS 攻击」。

items.content: 11 月 20 日，Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 在个人网站发布声明，称自己与 Claude 合作找到了黎曼猜想的证明，并表示同一方法还可以推广至广义黎曼猜想。目前，这一成果尚未经过独立验证。 黎曼猜想是数学界著名的「千禧年七大难题」之一，由德国数学家黎曼于 1859 年提出，涉及素数的分布规律。Alpöge 此次公开了一份 4 页说明，以及分成 14 个压缩包的 Lean 形式化证明文件，供其他研究者核查。 Alpöge 介绍，这项研究借鉴了数论中已有的证明思路，通过串联名为 theta 提升的数学变换，模拟传统方法中的「重数」作用。其中，Claude 提出让变换链的长度随求和范围的平方根增长，成为推进证明的关键思路之一。他表示，Claude 在研究后期的推进速度已经超过自己，接下来还将整理一份便于数学家理解的人类可读证明。 菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩也于 11 月 20 日在个人博客提及此事。他指出，Alpöge 使用 AI 生成了一份规模庞大、仅以 Lean 代码呈现的广义黎曼猜想证明，理解和消化这份成果仍需要时间，但至少可以与人类作者沟通，协助完成这一过程。 目前，数学界仍需确认这些 Lean 文件能否独立通过校验，以及形式化定理是否准确对应黎曼猜想。陶哲轩的回应也不意味着证明已经获得认可。 三星电子 11 月 20 日宣布，由崔元俊接掌负责 Galaxy 手机的移动体验业务，卢泰文继续领导设备体验部门，并与负责半导体部门的全永铉共同担任 CEO。崔元俊自 2025 年 3 月起担任移动体验业务 COO，曾负责推动 Galaxy S26 和 Galaxy Z Fold8 系列上市。

items.author: Aisha Malik
items.content: Jensen Huang is scheduled to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, according to a notice on the committee’s website. The development comes just hours after Huang was reinstated as Nvidia chief executive, less than two weeks following his resignation after it was revealed that he engaged in at least two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected by the U.S. government of working as a Chinese spy. The Senate Banking Committee has jurisdiction over export control policies that are designed to prevent sensitive U.S. technologies, such as chips capable of powering AI models, from falling into the hands of foreign governments and militaries. The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about his affair with the suspected Chinese spy and his potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations. It’s worth noting that before his reinstatement as CEO, Huang had already agreed to appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and the House Intelligence Committee on December 1. items.title: Amazon snaps up Decart’s AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
items.description: Amazon is acquiring Decart’s AI optimization technology and research team in a reported $7.5 billion deal.
items.author: Rebecca Bellan
items.content: Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart. The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg. Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models to run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware. As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post . “Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.” Amazon, which has been so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far.

Trump got his way, as Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement shortly afterwards. “I spoke to them, let me put it that way… And I convinced them,” the president told CNBC. items.title: OpenAI’s chief scientist has thoughts on how to limit AI development
items.description: To establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how to measure speed.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: A new blog post from OpenAI’s chief scientist Jakub Pachocki discusses potential limits on AI development, with a focus on a measurement called perplexity. Slowing AI development became a particularly hot topic after a former OpenAI and Anthropic researcher said the companies were “gambling with our lives,” and even Anthropic’s IPO filing suggested that the technology could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to society.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei then published a plan to “pace the frontier,” seemingly endorsed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Among other things, Amodei called for companies to agree to “common safety standards as well as limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress.” But to establish a speed limit on AI development, you need to agree on how you measure speed. Pachocki’s post — described by Altman as “the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while” — suggests perplexity (not to be confused with the company of the same name ) could be that measurement. In Pachocki’s argument, benchmarks that focus on AI’s “downstream capabilities” have quickly become outdated as the technology advances. But perplexity — which “measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions” — has remained “informative.” Pachocki’s post includes a chart of how the perplexity of OpenAI’s models has fallen since GPT-3.5.

items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: In his new book “Hyperscale,” journalist Paris Marx investigates the impact of data centers and generative AI, taking readers inside the data centers themselves and explaining how computing infrastructure that goes back decades recently became a political landmine. The book is well-timed, to put it mildly, as data center backlash seems to have been one of the motivators for the massive blue wave seen in the recent midterm elections . And those debates are likely to continue as Democrats wield more governmental power . items.title: Signal restricts mobile screenshots as it confronts ‘existential threat’ of AI surveillance
items.description: Signal is limiting users' ability to take screenshots in both its Android and iOS apps.
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: Signal announced Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI. Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” “Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.” Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS. items.title: Here are the top AI agents that can live in your text messages
items.description: We created a list of the most notable AI agents that can live in your text messages, from general assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work.
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content: Rather than downloading another app, a growing number of agents can simply be texted like an ordinary person. You text it what you need, and it can remember context, connect to the apps and services you already use, and complete tasks on your behalf. That can mean scheduling an appointment, organizing a calendar, researching a trip, sending an email, making a reservation, shopping online, or reminding you about something days later. While Instinct is one of the buzziest AI agents at present, thanks to its $10 billion valuation after its latest funding round of $1 billion, there are many others also making a play for this space. Below are the most notable options so far, from general-purpose personal assistants to agents designed for families, travel, and work. Ask Proxy ’s biggest differentiator is that it “thinks like a woman,” meaning it aims to anticipate your needs before you even ask, the company explains on its website. It works like a chatbot you can text like a friend, whether you need gift ideas, help planning an event, or recommendations for things to do that weekend. You can ask it to add important dates to your calendar, set reminders, or help with everyday decisions. You can also send it photos, like an empty table, to figure out how to decorate the table for a dinner party.
